/-!
# Erdős Problem 1121

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1121](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1121)
- [BeLi16] Bezdek, Károly and Litvak, Alexander E., *Packing convex bodies by cylinders*.
  Discrete Comput. Geom. (2016), 725-738.
- [GoGo45] Goodman, A. W. and Goodman, R. E., *A circle covering theorem*. Amer. Math. Monthly
  (1945), 494-498.
- [Ha47] Hadwiger, H., *Nonseparable convex systems*. Amer. Math. Monthly (1947), 583-585.
-/

namespace Erdos1121

open scoped EuclideanGeometry

/--
If $C_1,\ldots,C_n$ are circles in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no line
disjoint from all the circles divides them into two non-empty sets then the circles can be
covered by a circle of radius $r=\sum r_i$.

This is true, and was proved by Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] (whose proof also generalises to
higher dimensions). A generalisation to convex bodies was proved by Hadwiger [Ha47].

An alternative proof is given by Bezdek and Litvak [BeLi16].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1121.lean"]
theorem erdos_1121 {n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → ℝ²) (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : ℝ²) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : ℝ², (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i) := by
  sorry

/--
The proof of Goodman and Goodman [GoGo45] also generalises to higher dimensions: if
$B_1,\ldots,B_n$ are balls in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with radii $r_1,\ldots,r_n$ such that no hyperplane
disjoint from all the balls divides them into two non-empty sets then the balls can be covered by
a ball of radius $r=\sum r_i$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_1121.variants.higher_dimension {d n : ℕ} (c : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (r : Fin n → ℝ) (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i)
    (hsep : ∀ (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (t : ℝ), v ≠ 0 →
      (∀ i, ∀ p ∈ Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i), inner ℝ v p ≠ t) →
      (∀ i, inner ℝ v (c i) < t) ∨ (∀ i, t < inner ℝ v (c i))) :
    ∃ z : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d),
      (⋃ i, Metric.closedBall (c i) (r i)) ⊆ Metric.closedBall z (∑ i, r i) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1121

reformulations.difference: The source forbids a disjoint line separating the disks into two nonempty groups. Lean instead quantifies over nonzero normal vectors and offsets, requiring all centers to lie strictly on the same side whenever the corresponding line avoids every closed ball.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every affine line has the form {p | inner ℝ v p = t} with v ≠ 0. Positive radius ensures that each ball contains its center. By convexity and the intermediate value theorem, a ball disjoint from this line lies wholly in the open half-plane containing its center. Consequently, the center-sign disjunction is equivalent to there being no disjoint line with points of the union on both sides, which is precisely the source's nonseparability condition. The corresponding ↔ was proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean as Review1121.centerNS_iff_noSplit, for arbitrary dimension and nonnegative radii.

reformulations.difference: The higher-dimensional variant likewise expresses geometric nonseparability using signs of inner products at the centers rather than explicitly quantifying over separating hyperplanes and subfamilies.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: A nonzero normal vector and real offset represent an arbitrary affine hyperplane in finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Any closed ball avoiding the hyperplane lies entirely on one side, by convexity; its center determines that side. Thus all centers lying strictly on one side is equivalent to the absence of two nonempty groups separated by that hyperplane. Review1121.centerNS_iff_noSplit proves this equivalence uniformly in d and n, so it applies directly to this declaration.

review.notes:
Both declarations are faithful. Bezdek–Litvak explicitly use closed circular disks, including the convention that touching a disk disqualifies a separating line. Their bound 2R_K ≤ diam_NS(K) = 2∑r_i gives exactly the stated covering radius. The higher-dimensional ball statement is also explicitly confirmed by Bezdek–Lángi.

Lean checks passed for empty families, singleton families, dimension zero, an admissible two-ball family, two separated unit disks that fail hsep, and a tangent line that is not disjoint. The source records PROVED (LEAN), consistent with the metadata. The cited external proof was kernel-checked after one tactic compatibility edit from its v4.29.1 environment to the sandbox's v4.33.1; a wrapper deriving the exact repository statement also has only [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] as axioms.

The original 1945/1947 articles were unavailable in full; their bibliographic pages, the problem's exact LaTeX, the cited alternative proof, and the later mathematical restatement were sufficient to settle both declarations. The website's LaTeX bibliography misresolves the key Ha47 to Hall, but the file's explicit Hadwiger reference agrees with Bezdek–Litvak's bibliography; this is not a defect in the reviewed file. All experiments remained under /workspace/review/, and the target file still matches the specified commit.
